column1: # Vehicle settings explained (own words, for owners). Keys: info.<id> = what it does, when.<id> = when to change it.
# Sources: research in docs/ (official app strings for names only; texts written for PHEV Link).

column2: Chooses when the indicator stalk works: only with the car switched fully on, or also in accessory mode.
Change it if you want the indicators to work (or not) while the car is only in accessory mode.
When on, a light tap on the indicator stalk flashes the indicators three times, handy for changing lanes.
Turn it off if you get three flashes when you only meant a quick signal.
Sets how many times the indicators flash to confirm locking and unlocking with the remote or keyless system.
Change it if you want more, fewer or no confirmation flashes, for example to be discreet at night.
Chooses how the front wipers behave on the intermittent setting: a fixed pause, a pause you set, one that also follows road speed, or one driven by the rain sensor.
Pick the speed- or rain-linked mode if you want the wipers to adjust themselves, or the fixed mode for predictable wiping.
Decides whether the wipers sweep automatically when you spray washer fluid, and whether they do one extra wipe a few seconds later to clear drips.
Choose the delayed-wipe option if washer fluid runs down the screen after washing.
Sets the pause between sweeps of the rear wiper on its intermittent setting (0 seconds means it wipes non-stop).
Use a longer pause in light drizzle and a shorter one in heavier rain.
Sets how long the small light inside the charging port stays on before switching itself off.
Lengthen it if you often plug in in the dark; shorten it if you want to spare the 12 V battery.
Controls whether and when the door mirrors fold and unfold by themselves, for example when you lock and unlock or as you drive off.
Change it if you want the mirrors folded away automatically when parked, or want them to stop moving on their own.
Sets how dark it has to get before the automatic headlights switch on.
Choose an earlier setting if the lights come on too late at dusk, or a later one if they come on too readily.
With the light switch on AUTO, switches the headlights on when the front wipers are running.
Turn it on if you want the headlights on automatically whenever it rains.
Sets how long the interior light stays on after you shut the doors.
Lengthen it for more time to buckle up or find things in the dark; shorten it to save the battery.
Switches the headlights and/or tail lights off by themselves if they are left on after the car is switched off and the driver's door is opened.
Only turn it off if you deliberately want the lights to stay on when parked; otherwise it protects the 12 V battery.
Switches the interior lights off automatically if they are left on with the car off, after the chosen time.
Shorten it to protect the 12 V battery, or turn it off if you need the lights on for long periods (camping, loading).
Sets how long you must hold the indicator stalk lightly before it counts as a three-flash lane-change signal.
Pick 'Long' if you trigger the three flashes by accident, 'Short' if they are hard to trigger.
Lets a single pull of the washer lever spray and wipe automatically, without holding the lever.
Turn it on if you want one-touch screen washing.
Unlocks the doors by itself when you shift into P or switch the car off (optionally only when the window-lock switch is off).
Turn it on for convenience when getting out; keep it off if you want the doors to stay locked until you choose.
Chooses whether one press of unlock opens all the doors or only the driver's door (a second press opens the rest).
Choose driver's door only for extra security if you often travel alone.
Sets whether deadlocking (the extra-secure lock that also disables the inside door handles) needs two presses of the lock button or one.
Change it if you want one-press deadlocking, or want to avoid deadlocking by accident with people inside.
Makes the horn give a short chirp when you lock with the remote: on every lock, only in daylight, only on a second press, or never.
Turn it off or limit it to daytime if the chirp disturbs neighbours.
Chooses whether the car beeps to confirm locking and unlocking with the keyless (touch-the-handle) system, the remote, both or neither.
Turn it off for silent locking, or on if you want to hear that the car really locked.
If you unlock with the remote but don't open a door, the car locks itself again after this time.
Lengthen it if the car relocks before you reach it.
Turns the factory theft alarm on or off.
Keep it on for protection; turn it off only if you have a reason, such as frequent false alarms.
Sets how long the electric windows (and sunroof, if fitted) keep working after you switch the car off.
Lengthen it if you often close the windows after switching off.
Appears to set how long the alarm's first warning stage lasts before the full alarm goes off.
Shorten it if you want the full alarm sooner.
Lets you open or close the windows and/or fold the mirrors by holding the remote's lock or unlock button.
Turn it on if you want to air the car or close forgotten windows from outside.
Appears to allow the remote's panic function to set off the alarm on purpose, to scare someone off or attract attention.
Turn it off if it is set off by accident.
Chooses a short or long horn chirp when the horn confirms locking.
Choose 'Short' to be less disruptive.
When you select reverse, the rear wiper gives a sweep: either only when the rear wiper is on, or when either the front or the rear wiper is on.
Choose the front-or-rear option for a clear rear window when reversing in rain.
Nobody has documented this one yet: Mitsubishi's app never names it (in any language), and neither do the manuals or forums. Your car offers it, so it does something.
Leave it as it is unless you want to experiment: note the current option first, and change it back if anything behaves differently.
Right after you lock, the remote and keyless unlock are ignored for a few seconds, so an accidental press doesn't unlock the car.
Turn it on if you sometimes unlock by mistake just after locking.
Sounds the horn when the engine is started remotely, on cars with a remote engine start.
Only relevant on cars with remote engine start.
Appears to control whether the windows can still be opened, not just closed, during the window timer after you switch off.
Turn it off if you only want to be able to close windows after switching off.
Sets which windows the window-lock button affects: all doors, or only the driver's door. Mitsubishi's own descriptions of this disagree, so check the effect after changing it.
Change it if the window lock blocks more or fewer windows than you want.
Turns accessory power (radio, sockets) off automatically after 30 or 60 minutes if the car is left in accessory mode.
Turn it on to avoid a flat 12 V battery if the car is sometimes left in accessory mode.
Nobody has documented this one yet: Mitsubishi's app never names it (in any language), and neither do the manuals or forums. Your car offers it, so it does something.
Leave it as it is unless you want to experiment: note the current option first, and change it back if anything behaves differently.
Nobody has documented this one yet: Mitsubishi's app never names it (in any language), and neither do the manuals or forums. Your car offers it, so it does something.
Leave it as it is unless you want to experiment: note the current option first, and change it back if anything behaves differently.
Appears to set how easily the alarm's interior movement (intrusion) sensor is triggered, from Level 1 (most sensitive) to Level 4 (least).
Lower it if the alarm goes off by itself (insects, air movement, a sunshade moving).
Keeps the headlights on for a while after you switch off and get out, to light your way ('coming home' lights).
Choose a longer time if you park somewhere dark.
Switches on the parking lights or headlights when you unlock with the remote, to help you find and reach the car.
Turn it on for dark car parks, off to be discreet or save battery.
Lets the climate system switch between fresh outside air and recirculated air by itself, or leaves it to you.
Choose 'Manual' if you want full control, for example to keep traffic fumes out.
Lets the climate system switch the air-conditioning compressor on and off by itself, or leaves it to you.
Choose 'Manual' to save energy if you rarely need cooling or dehumidifying.
Chooses whether the climate system favours saving energy (Eco) or comfort.
Pick 'Eco' for more electric range, 'Comfort' for faster heating and cooling.
When air blows to both the feet and the windscreen, shifts the balance between the two.
Send more to the windscreen if it mists up, or more to the feet if they get cold.
When air blows to both the face and the feet, shifts the balance between the two.
Adjust to taste, for example more to the feet in winter.
Switches the rear-window demister on by itself when you start the car.
Turn it on if you usually need it in winter, off to save energy.
Starts the air conditioning or heater by itself when you unlock the doors, so the cabin is warming or cooling as you get in.
Turn it on for a more comfortable start in hot or cold weather.
In feet-only mode, lets a little air flow to the windscreen to help keep it clear.
Turn it on if the windscreen mists up in feet mode.
Lets the engine run faster while stationary so the heater gets more warmth.
Turn it on in very cold weather if the heater feels weak while standing still.
